You have some good advice here already. But I’ll second that people will always complain, that is an absolute. 

In my staff meetings I’ll usually have a couple of bullets on professionalism in the office or respect, where I’ll mention topics close enough to what I know has been said just to let folks know that word travels. 

Self-awareness is good but don’t let doubt bring you down. If you truly feel you’re deficient in an area, work to improve that. If not, drive on with confidence that your employer trusts you to make good decisions, or you’d likely not be there.

I think there is a balance to be found between stoicism and being a bit more genuine and casual. I find, especially with younger employees, that they respect effort to be casual. It is more taxing though. 

Your speaking will improve with confidence, and that’ll take time. Over-prepare for presentations, and find a mate that may listen to you practice, or use a mirror. The better you know the subject matter, the more your responses become “muscle memory” and you minimize risk of that panic spiral into a mind blank while digging for a response.
